title: Fit an inside-bolt-circle gasket: far bolts first as stops, then the near bolts
instruction: Fit the gasket between the flanges, centred on the pipe, put all four bolts in and let go.
context: Pipefitters fitting an inside-bolt-circle gasket put the far bolts in first, slide the gasket in until it rests against them, which centres it, then add the near bolts; with all bolts in first the gasket cannot pass the near pair, and an off-centre gasket leaks. Done by: pipefitters (O*NET 47-2152.00). Closest look-alike: TK-YEYBRK. Unlike TK-25G7NE and TK-D86EB3 (order set by bore sizes), the first fasteners become the gasket's stops.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Pipe axis: vertical, 34.0 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline. Lower flange (fixed, grey steel): 160 x 160 mm, 15 mm thick, lying on the table centred on the pipe axis and square to the table, with a 60 mm square bore in its middle and four 16 mm square clearance holes. Upper flange (fixed, grey steel): the same outline, 10 mm thick, level, 35 to 45 mm above the table, with the same bore and four 13 mm square bolt holes; it is held up by two 12 x 12 mm dark steel posts at its far edge, 65 mm either side of the midline, leaving a 20 mm gap between the flanges (15 to 35 mm high). The four holes in each flange are centred on a 65 mm-radius circle round the pipe axis, at 46.0 mm in front of and behind the axis and 46.0 mm left and right of it: two far holes and two near holes. Support block (fixed, tan wood): 135 x 140 mm, 15 mm tall, its far edge against the near edge of the lower flange. Gasket (loose, black rubber, 25 g): a flat ring 4 mm thick, outer radius 59.5 mm and inner radius 40.5 mm (edges slightly scalloped, 0.6 mm), with a handle tab 20 mm wide and 10 mm tall reaching 85 mm out of its edge toward the robot; it lies flat on the support block, its centre 19.5 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline. Bolts (loose, bright steel, 30 g each): a 10 mm shank 42 mm long under a head 20 mm across and 10 mm tall, four standing upright on their shank ends on the table, 20.0 cm in front of the arm bases, at 15.0 and 21.0 cm left and right of the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: From a photo from above, a ruler and the video. Still means moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s. The gasket is in when it lies flat on the lower flange (its underside within 1.5 mm of the flange's top and tilted less than 3 degrees) with its centre within 4 mm of the pipe axis, still, and no gripper within 5 mm of it. The flange hides the gasket, so its centre is found from the tab, which stays in view: it is the point 144.5 mm behind the tab's end along the tab's centre line (centred, the tab's end is 64.5 mm in front of the flange's near edge, on the midline). A bolt is in a hole when it stands within 8 degrees of upright, its head's underside within 2 mm of the upper flange's top, its head's centre within 3 mm of the hole's centre seen from above, still, with no gripper within 5 mm of it. Score 1.0: the gasket is in and all four holes have a bolt in. Score 0.5: the gasket is in and both far holes have a bolt in, but not all four holes. Score 0 in every other case, including all four bolts in with the gasket outside, the gasket in with only the near bolts, and the gasket not centred. A trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the last step.
reset_notes: Take out all four bolts and stand them on the table at their marks; slide the gasket back onto the support block, flat, its tab pointing at the robot. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Flanges and holes are square-cut steel boxes and the gasket is a rigid ring of overlapping discs, not soft rubber; there are no nuts, threads or torque, and seating is judged by position. The bolts are 10 mm plain rods. The gap is held open by fixed posts rather than a spread flange. Friction is the simulator's grippy default (1.2). The layout is fixed, so a memorised sequence for this one layout cannot be ruled out.
